newsitem.title: UK: UK MPs to see sleaze report next week.
newsitem.headline: UK MPs to see sleaze report next week.

text.p: UK Parliament's ethics commissioner, Sir Gordon Downey, will present his report on "cash for questions" allegations involving former Conservative member of parliament Neil Hamilton to MPs next week, ministers said on Thursday.

They said Downey would attend the first meeting in the current parliament of the powerful House of Commons Standards and Privileges Committee, which is expected to discuss a date for publishing the report.
Downey had hoped to publish the report into Hamilton and nine other MPs and former MPs before the election campaign got under way, but it was not quite ready in time.
Because the work of Commons committees ended when parliament was prorogued, the report could not be published and has been kept under lock and key since then.

In a charge that ministers stand by, Labour maintained at the time that former prime minister John Major called the May 1 election unusually early to delay publication of the potentially embarrassing report. Major called the charge nonsense.

Hamilton, a former trade minister, has strongly denied allegations that he accepted cash from the Egyptian-born owner of Harrods department store, Mohammed Al-Fayed, in return for asking questions in parliament.
Hamilton lost his seat at the election to an anti-sleaze candidate, former BBC war reporter Martin Bell.
In an ironic footnote, ministers said they were planning to expand membership of the Standards and Privileges Committee to include Bell once it had finished work on the Hamilton case.
